products.name: Langfuse
products.note: Open-source, framework-agnostic LLM observability: tracing, prompt management, evals, datasets; OpenTelemetry-native; acquired by ClickHouse

profile_text.body:
Langfuse is an open-source AI engineering platform designed to help teams build, monitor, and improve applications built on large language models. The company describes itself as the most widely adopted open-source LLM engineering platform, reporting use by 50,000 or more companies and processing billions of observations per month. Its platform covers tracing, prompt management, evaluations, and analytics dashboards across the full development lifecycle, and is built to be framework-agnostic and OpenTelemetry-native.

The core product, also called Langfuse, captures hierarchical traces of every LLM call, tool invocation, and retrieval step, allowing teams to filter by user, session, cost, latency, or custom metadata. The site lists integrations with a wide range of tools and frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, LiteLLM, Dify, Langflow, Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Agent Framework, AutoGen, and others. Langfuse positions its approach as distinct from traditional observability platforms, arguing that LLM systems produce rich, verbose input and output at each step that legacy tools cannot handle at enterprise scale.

The held facts note that Langfuse has been acquired by ClickHouse, which also appears among the listed integrations on the company's site. No litigation, SEC filings, patents, or MCP server registrations are recorded for the company.
